answers.b: A high-performance networking standard for low-latency communication

explanations.b: Correct. InfiniBand provides low-latency, high-bandwidth networking for HPC.

questions.question: Q2 What is a network topology?

answers.a: The physical arrangement and connection pattern of network nodes
answers.b: The speed of a network connection
answers.c: The number of GPUs in a system

explanations.a: Correct. Topology describes how nodes are interconnected.

questions.question: Q3 How many hops does a Fat-Tree topology require between any two nodes?

explanations.c: Correct. Fat-Tree limits hops to exactly 4 regardless of cluster size.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Fat-Tree has fixed hops, unlike 3D Torus.

answers.a: Time to convert data from parallel to serial format for transmission
answers.b: Time for a GPU to boot up
answers.c: Time to store data on disk

explanations.a: Correct. It is the time to place data onto the network link.

questions.question: Q5 What is the bandwidth of InfiniBand NDR?

explanations.c: Correct. NDR provides 400 Gbps per port.

questions.question: Q6 In a 3D Torus, how are the routing hops calculated?

explanations.c: Correct. Hops scale with the cube root of the node count.

questions.question: Q7 What is a 'hop' in networking?

answers.b: A single link traversal through a switch or router

explanations.b: Correct. Each hop represents passing through one intermediate network device.

questions.question: Q8 Why does 3D Torus have lower cabling cost than Fat-Tree?

answers.b: Each node connects only to its nearest neighbors

explanations.b: Correct. Each node has a fixed number of connections (6 neighbors), reducing total cabling.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Switches may still be involved.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Cable length is not the primary factor.

answers.d: The bandwidth of the fastest switch
